dedupe_keys.name: public charging requirements for battery electric long haul trucks in europe trip chain approach

description: This dataset gives the charger locations, break and rest points and energy and power requirements estimated for battery electric trucks in long-haul operation (over 4.5 hours or 360 km) in Europe in 2030. A trip chain model converts the ETISplus annual origin-destination flows of goods by heavy-duty vehicles between NUTS-3 regions into routes, places short breaks and long rests along them according to EU driving time rules, and aggregates stops into 25 by 25 km charging areas; for 15 percent of long-haul trucks being electric it estimates about 40,000 overnight charging points (50 to 100 kW) and 9,000 megawatt charging points. It was produced at Chalmers University of Technology by Shoman, Yeh, Sprei and Plötz, released in several versions from October 2022. Coverage is continental at NUTS-3 and charging-area level for the 2030 horizon. Shapefiles of charger locations and of rest and break points (about 540 MB) are free on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: results rest on assumed truck penetration and a simple queuing model, and regional differences and truck heterogeneity are not modelled. The data support capacity planning of truck charging corridors and network flow studies of electric road freight, and relate to ETISplus and to the European truck charging demand results catalogued here.
name: Public charging requirements for battery electric long-haul trucks in Europe (trip chain approach)
provider: Chalmers University of Technology (Wasim Shoman, Sonia Yeh, Frances Sprei) and Patrick Plötz
